solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leaders in Pondicherry pardon an Indian

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening pair of letters of the Indian city's name is taken

parts.note: 'Pardon?' and 'What?' are both ways of asking someone to repeat themselves

explanation.surface: A request for forgiveness is addressed to a man in the former French enclave of Pondicherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' is plural here, so take the first two letters, PO. 'Indian' looks like it describes someone in Pondicherry, but the answer is a Native American chief from Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: Powhatan was a paramount chief of the Native American people of Virginia, the father of Pocahontas.

clue.text: Dominant and aware of power

parts.note: to be onto something is to have become aware of it
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone in charge who also knows how power works.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the superior position, or having the upper hand, is the idiomatic sense of being dominant.

clue.text: Prudent compromise pleased spiritualist

parts.note: pleased is a synonym of happy
a medium is a spiritualist who claims to contact the dead

explanation.surface: A sensible middle way leaves the clairvoyant contented.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a sensible middle course between two extremes, which is a prudent compromise.

clue.text: Problem for divers — no diving at first in ancient city

indicators.note: the two initial letters are placed inside the city's name

parts.note: Thebes was an ancient city in both Egypt and Greece

indicators.note: 'at first' asks for the initial letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A ban on diving in an ancient city poses a problem for divers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the initial letters of 'no diving' inside the ancient city, which here is Greek or Egyptian Thebes rather than any modern place.
explanation.definitionFit: Decompression sickness, which strikes divers who surface too fast, is known by this colloquial name.

clue.text: Sort of threatening show that surprises me

indicators.note: to sort something is to arrange it, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes an alarming kind of performance that has caught them off guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges THREATENING and SHOW together, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a colloquial expression of mild astonishment at something unexpected.

clue.text: Make fast dog check out

indicators.note: 'out' here means outside, so the word for check goes round the dog

parts.note: to see that something is done is to check it
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Tie up the dog quickly and then inspect it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' tells you SEE goes outside CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure a rope or a door is to make it fast, fixing it firmly in place.

clue.text: Imprisoning sweetheart, Solomon is just

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding something inside, so the name goes round the letter

parts.note: Solly is a familiar short form of the name Solomon
the heart, or middle letter, of the word sweet is E

explanation.surface: Solomon, holding his beloved captive, is said to be fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is read as sweet's heart, the middle letter E, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Solely and just both mean only or merely, as in 'just for fun'.

clue.text: Fleece from one in pen?

definitions.meaning: to fleece is to swindle or cheat someone out of money
a pen is slang for a penitentiary, so one in it is a convict, shortened

explanation.surface: Wool taken from a sheep kept in its enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sheep in a sheep pen; in fact the pen is a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A con is a swindle, a way to fleece someone, and also short for convict.

clue.text: Doctor getting substance right in the end

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the word for the end

parts.note: the rear is the back end of something
the gist is the substance or essence of a matter

explanation.surface: A doctor finally grasps the essence of a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts GISTR inside REAR. 'Doctor' looks like a verb, but it is the hospital rank.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a doctor in training ranking just below a consultant.

clue.text: Principal means of keeping papers together

definitions.meaning: a ... diet or ... crop is the main or principal one
a bent wire fastener driven through sheets of paper

explanation.definitionFit: Staple means chief or basic as an adjective, and is also a wire fastener for paper.

clue.text: Almost consider keeping £50 note

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the word for consider goes round the rest

parts.note: to weigh a matter is to consider it
L is the sign for pound sterling (libra) and L is the Roman numeral for fifty
N is taken as an abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: Someone nearly decides to keep a fifty-pound banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts LLN inside WEIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-nigh is a slightly old-fashioned adverb meaning nearly or very close to.

clue.text: Active agent overcoming resistance

indicators.note: overcoming is read as coming over, the agent covering the letter

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An energetic secret agent defeats the Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcoming' puts R inside SPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means lively and nimble, especially of an older person, so it describes someone active.

clue.text: Desmond Morris, for example, got the oils out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: The zoologist Desmond Morris took the oil paints out.
explanation.walkthrough: Desmond Morris, author of The Naked Ape, was also a surrealist painter, hence the oils. 'out' rearranges GOT THE OILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Desmond Morris is a zoologist who studies animal behaviour, which is the field of the scientist named here.

clue.text: Like curate's egg but no ham?

definitions.meaning: a curate's egg is something partly good and partly bad, after a Punch cartoon of a meek curate served a bad egg
an actor who is no ham performs his roles well

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an egg breakfast without the ham; but a ham is a bad actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something mixed, as the curate said of his egg, and an actor who does roles well.

clue.text: Bad-tempered woman depicted by Titian, perhaps, turning more artful

parts.note: a shrew is a scolding, bad-tempered woman

indicators.note: turning means the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: Titian is a shade of auburn red, named after the painter's favoured hair colour

explanation.surface: A painting by Titian shows a bad-tempered woman becoming craftier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes DER from RED. Titian looks like the painter, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewder is the comparative of shrewd, meaning sharper or more cunning, which is more artful.

clue.text: On a trip, even involving very important people

parts.note: someone on a drug trip is high
even means flat or level

explanation.surface: Someone on holiday is drawn into dealings with VIPs.
explanation.definitionFit: High-level talks or meetings are those involving senior, important people.

clue.text: Vegetable needing fine rain? Not half!

parts.note: OK means all right or fine

indicators.note: only half of the word rain is kept, the first two letters

explanation.surface: A vegetable crop that needs a gentle drizzle, and the answer comes back: not half!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is a British exclamation meaning 'very much so'; here it keeps only half of 'rain', RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a green pod vegetable, also called ladies' fingers or gumbo.

clue.text: His trade could be most likely to survive

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A tradesman's line of work may be the one most likely to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges HIS TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: The hardiest plant or person is the toughest, best able to endure harsh conditions.

clue.text: 20, so to speak, for fruit

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word is to be said rather than written

parts.note: 20 refers to the answer at 20-down, which taken as the opposite of fair-looking means plain or ugly

explanation.surface: A cross-reference leads, in a manner of speaking, to a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 20-down's answer as 'not fair' in looks. The fruit is a Jamaican citrus hybrid, named for its knobbly skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a hybrid of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: European resort empty in recession

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: recession means going back, so the word for empty is read backwards

parts.note: to drain a vessel is to empty it

explanation.surface: A holiday resort lies deserted during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' turns DRAIN into NIARD. 'empty' looks like an adjective describing the resort, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is a native of Spain, so is a European.

clue.text: Where rides are not beginning? That's not cricket!

indicators.note: the beginning, or first letter, is removed from the word

parts.note: fairground rides are found at a funfair

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a fairground's rides have not started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not cricket' is a British idiom for unsporting or unjust behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something not cricket means it is unsporting, an idiom for an unjust act.

clue.text: On cloud nine? About one minute out

indicators.note: about means around, so the happy word goes round the other two

parts.note: to be on cloud nine is to be extremely happy, or elated
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone euphoric is knocked out of a contest almost immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts IMIN inside ELATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who is out of a competition has been knocked out, or removed from it.

clue.text: Quiet time for young attendant

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A peaceful interval for a young attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a boy employed as a personal attendant, or a young wedding attendant.

clue.text: Information that is a means of wish-fulfilment

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Knowing the facts is the way to get what you want.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie, as in the Aladdin story, grants wishes to whoever releases it from its lamp.

clue.text: Sinister character for whom Vangelis composed?

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the composer's name is put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A villain for whom the composer Vangelis wrote a score?
explanation.walkthrough: Vangelis is a Greek composer of film scores; 'composed' rearranges his name. Svengali is the sinister hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the hypnotist in Trilby, is a sinister manipulator, and his name now means any such person.

clue.text: Novel recognised when read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud means the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: recognised means knew, as in 'I knew him at once'

explanation.surface: A book is recognised when someone reads it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel as an adjective means fresh or not seen before, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Wrong band to follow Queen

indicators.note: to follow says the band word comes after the queen's letters

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: It was a mistake for a band to follow the rock group Queen on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock group; it is the monarch's cipher ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Erring means going astray or making a mistake, so doing wrong.

clue.text: Phone bishop's subordinate

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
lower means junior or subordinate in rank

explanation.surface: Call the bishop's junior clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the blower' is old British slang for the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Blower is British slang for a telephone, so it can stand for phone.

clue.text: Visit would shortly deteriorate

parts.note: to visit someone is to go to see them
would is shortened to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: Someone who would pay a call does so only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would shortly' is the contraction 'd.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to seed is an idiom, from plants bolting, meaning to decline or deteriorate.
